coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Walk (335 Berry St)
record.summary: Mission Walk is a below-market-rate for-sale condominium development at 330 and 335 Berry St in Mission Bay North; this building (335 Berry St) was completed in 2009 per DataSF Assessor records (a 2023 city memo likewise lists Mission Walk as 131 family for-sale units completed in 2009, a development-wide year), and a lottery for the development's 131 BMR units was announced in 2008 for January 28, 2009.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8707120 (2,696 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 67 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8707120 and 66 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8707120)); 97% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 67% of the lot.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 8707120 (mapped 2010-01-11; active); the earlier outline came from: DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8707120); name/address from OpenStreetMap way 56656114 (335 Berry St)

facts.value: Sources differ (131 across Mission Walk, or 80 condos at 330 and 335 Berry)

changes.text: In October 2008 SocketSite reported that applications were open for the 131 below-market-rate condos that "will compose Mission Walk (330/335 Berry Street)", with a lottery set for January 28, 2009. The post says the site "might still be wrapped in scaffolding" and does not say how far construction had gone.

Long 'At a glance' values were cut to the fact itself (or 'Sources differ'); the disputes, quoted excerpts and hedging moved to this record's open questions, with every source still named. No change to the record's status or shape.
The summary for Mission Walk (335 Berry St) now includes a 2023 city memo on completion year.
Mission Walk (335 Berry St) now uses its Assessor lot lines.
The Mission Walk (335 Berry St) page now lists the sources its text relies on: San Francisco Condo Market, the Assessor roll and SocketSite's October 2008 post, alongside OpenStreetMap.

The record said Mission Walk was built under the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency's Affordable Homeownership Program and that its below-market units were allocated by a lottery in January 2009. Neither cited source says the first, and SocketSite (2008) only announced the lottery for January 28, 2009, so the summary now says that. A 2023 city memo listing Mission Walk as 131 family for-sale affordable units completed in 2009 is now cited. The map notes said the opening year and unit count were unconfirmed; they now state the 2009 build year (Assessor and Condo Market SF) and that the unit count for this address alone is unsettled. The aerial photo credit names the Commons account Firstcultural (Alfred Twu, per its user page) and drops the unsupported 'departing flight' wording.

open_questions: Precise completion month in 2009 is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year.

DataSF Assessor's own use_code/unit-count fields for this specific parcel (Single Family Residential, 0 units, 2 stories) look like a condo common-element or garage lot rather than the full building, while listing sites describe a larger residential building at this address; not reconciled here.

Unit count: SocketSite (October 27, 2008) says 131 below-market-rate condos "will compose Mission Walk (330/335 Berry Street)" (25 one-, 82 two- and 24 three-bedroom units), but San Francisco Condo Market describes 330 Berry St as "a 41-unit condominium building" and 335 Berry St as "a 39-unit condominium building", 80 units in all, which is fewer than 131. Which figure describes the two buildings is not settled by any source read: the 131 may include units elsewhere in the Mission Walk program (a 2023 city memo lists 131 units on Blocks N4-A and N4-A2), or the listing site's counts may be incomplete.
Developer/architect not confirmed from any source checked as of 2026-09-21.
